text:
leo: FYI seeing a jump in fncall rejects in the us-east-1 canary. Error is `extra_properties` from strict schema. small sample:
```
{
  "error": "extra_properties",
  "found_keys": ["metadata", "debug_info"],
  "validator": "strict-output-v3"
}
```
Can we triage? tagging @sophia @maya

sophia: Noted. Does infra have the rollout metadata for strict-output-v3? Need region + percent. Also we keep losing `account_id` in the event when validation errors happen before routing. Makes it hard to tie to customers.

infra-bot: Canary status: feature=strict-output-v3, region=us-east-1, rollout_pct=7, status=running

maya: Two quick questions: 1) Do we want to soft-accept unknown fields and attach a `schema_extra` bag instead of rejecting? 2) If we soft-accept, do we flag the event so billing/quotas know it was a soft-accept?

derek: I'm cautious. Soft-accept reduces customer breakage but can hide bugs. If we soft-accept we must: a) add explicit event flags: `schema_mode=soft_accept`, `orig_error=extra_properties`, `route_id` and `account_id` included; b) increment a new metric `fncall.schema.soft_accepts` separately from rejects.

sophia: Agree. Also we should standardize error codes: EXTRA_FIELDS, MISSING_REQUIRED, TYPE_MISMATCH, UNPARSEABLE. Right now logs vary across validators.

leo: The spike seems concentrated on a few API keys. I can pull full payload samples, but note privacy: payloads may have PII. Need redact rules.

maya: Console UX: when a user's request hits a validation error, do we show the original request snippet in the console error panel? We probably shouldn't show PII unless account has explicit permission. Maybe show a redacted snippet and a button to request a full sample (requires audit log access).

derek: For immediate mitigation: flip strict-output-v3 to soft-accept in the canary + annotate canary with `soft-accept-temp=true`. That buys time for telemetry + redaction.

infra-bot: Update applied: strict-output-v3 -> SOFT-ACCEPT, rollout_pct->3 in us-east-1. Change logged by deploy-user on 2024-05-15T14:12:30Z

sophia: I'll file a telemetry PR to add `schema_mode`, `orig_error`, `account_id` to validation events and create a dashboard panel: "schema soft-accepts by account" + top offending keys list. Will add sampling for full payloads at 3% and ensure redaction pipeline runs. PR: https://git.internal/repo/telemetry/PR-210

leo: Can we also ensure billing attribution doesn't change? Right now soft-accepts route to the degen chain and increment a different counter. That's confusing for customers.

maya: Good point. New policy: soft-accept should preserve original route/quota attribution. We will add `soft_accept_override_route=true` flag so quota system attributes to original route. Add INF-4902 to implement.

derek: I'll do the temp toggle rollback plan in the playbook. We should also surface a console notice for affected customers with recommended fixes (e.g., remove `metadata` top-level key or move to `context`). Draft message: "Your request included unexpected top-level properties which are now accepted but may be rejected in future releases. See INF-4902 for details."

leo: Creating INF-4902 and linking PR. I'll attach sample redacted payloads.

maya: Action summary: derek flips soft-accept (done), sophia telemetry + dashboard, leo customer sampling + ticket, derek playbook + console notice. Timeline: telemetry + dashboard in 4h, console notice draft by EOD.

sophia: I'll include schema enum and conversion mapping in PR. Also adding unit tests for validator to ensure stable error codes.

maya: OK closing thread. Keep updates in INF-4902. :thumbsup:
